source_text.body:
Plan a Kickstarter launch and manage PR with an agent
A user running OpenClaw on an old laptop says it designed their Kickstarter go-to-market strategy and manages their PR pipeline; another user's bot phoned local businesses.
·
Feb 4, 2026
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
The Tom's Guide piece only quotes a user's post. That user runs OpenClaw on a 13-year-old HP laptop with Ubuntu and says it designed their whole Kickstarter go-to-market strategy and manages their PR pipeline. OpenClaw runs locally and takes instructions by text through messaging apps. The article gives no setup details, prompts or workflow. Separately, an X user had their bot call local businesses and posted the recordings.
How it went
The user claims the agent replaced what would have been a five-person team. That is a self-reported claim with no figures, and the article doesn't check it. It also doesn't say how the Kickstarter turned out.
Worth knowing
Tom's Guide warns that OpenClaw is a security risk and advises running it in a sandbox, away from sensitive data and your main messaging accounts.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
I'm launching [product] on [Kickstarter/other platform] to [target audience] with a goal of [funding goal] and a launch date of [date]. Draft a go-to-market plan covering pre-launch audience building, launch week, and the final push, plus a list of [number] publications or creators to pitch with a short pitch email for each. Present it as a week-by-week checklist and stop there; don't send anything.
Original source: https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/openclaw-is-the-viral-ai-assistant-that-lives-on-your-device-what-you-need-to-know
